title: TrumpFile Attributes Mogilevich–Putin Remarks to an Unverified 2000 Conversation
description_short: TrumpFile attributes remarks about Semion Mogilevich and Vladimir Putin to a 2000 Kuchma–Derkach conversation; no Trump connection is shown.
description_medium: TrumpFile’s timeline dates an excerpt to February 8, 2000, and attributes the private conversation to Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma and security chief Leonid Derkach, reportedly recorded by Mykola Melnychenko. In the excerpt, Derkach is quoted as describing contact between Semion Mogilevich and Vladimir Putin. The supplied research notes say the recording’s authenticity has not been independently verified. The accessed page excerpt does not mention Donald Trump or establish a Trump connection.
description_long: This internal draft describes what TrumpFile’s timeline page reports, not an authenticated recording or an independently verified historical event. The page dates its excerpt to February 8, 2000, attributes the private conversation to Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma and security-service head Leonid Derkach, and identifies Mykola Melnychenko as the recorder. It quotes Derkach as saying that Semion Mogilevich was on good terms with Vladimir Putin and that the two had been in contact since Putin was in Leningrad. TrumpFile says journalist J. V. Koshiw obtained the transcript and published it in a book. The supplied prior research notes caution that the recording’s authenticity has not been independently verified; the accessed page itself does not provide an authentication record. The excerpt does not mention Donald Trump, and the packet supplies no evidence connecting this conversation to him. The original human-rights and immigration classification is unsupported by this material. Keep the entry unpublished unless a credible source verifies the recording and a separate source establishes a direct or indirect Trump connection.
date_precision: day as displayed by TrumpFile; underlying event unverified

title: Supplied Record Alleges Emergency-Funding Redirections and Impoundment Disputes
description_short: The supplied record alleges a February 2025 funding-redirection pattern, but its GAO, court, date, and project claims remain unverified.
description_medium: The frozen entry alleges that in February 2025 Trump used several emergency declarations to redirect appropriated money to border, defense, and deportation priorities, followed by GAO findings and court injunctions. The packet includes no supporting decisions, cases, or underlying records. A March 2025 Congressional Research Service sidebar describes January 20 border and energy emergencies under 10 U.S.C. § 2808; that contextual account does not verify this composite claim.
description_long: This internal draft preserves the frozen entry’s allegation without presenting its composite account as established. The entry says that in February 2025 President Donald Trump invoked several national-emergency declarations to redirect congressionally appropriated funds toward border construction, defense spending, and deportation operations. It further claims that the Government Accountability Office found multiple redirections unlawful and that federal courts issued injunctions. The supplied packet identifies no specific GAO decisions, court cases, appropriations accounts, transfer amounts, or orders supporting those assertions. The Congressional Research Service’s March 11, 2025 legal sidebar reports that Trump declared southern-border and national-energy emergencies on January 20 and invoked 10 U.S.C. § 2808 concerning military-construction funding. That is relevant background, but it does not establish the frozen entry’s February 15 composite event, its claims about several funding streams, or its GAO and court outcomes. Do not replace the original event with the separate January 20 actions or state illegality, injunctions, or project effects as fact. Keep the date and claims attributed to the supplied record and unpublished until each action is identified and sourced.

title: Supplied March 15 Claim That Trump Called the Judiciary ‘Rigged’ Remains Unverified
description_short: The supplied record’s March 15 claim about a ‘rigged’ federal judiciary is unverified; a March 14 transcript contains narrower criticism of some judges.
description_medium: The frozen entry says Trump declared on March 15, 2025, that the federal judiciary was rigged against him, then combines that statement with first-term appointment totals and claims about judges blocking later orders. The packet did not verify the exact statement or count. An official transcript of March 14 Justice Department remarks records criticism of some judges, but does not establish the asserted March 15 wording or broader claim.
description_long: This internal draft keeps the frozen record’s specific assertion attributed and unpublished. The record says that on March 15, 2025, Donald Trump declared the entire federal judicial system “rigged against” him and links that alleged statement to his first-term appointments and rulings blocking second-term executive orders. The supplied prior research did not verify that exact statement and notes that the entry combines it with separate claims about the bench and particular judges. An official GovInfo transcript of Trump’s March 14 Justice Department remarks records him saying he had seen “some of the most corrupt judges” while discussing people he praised at the department. That transcript is adjacent context only: it neither documents a March 15 statement that the whole federal judiciary was rigged against him nor substantiates the entry’s count of 234 judicial appointments or its claims about which judges blocked orders. Do not treat those remarks as confirmation of the frozen statement or replace it with a different event. title: Lawsuit Alleges ICE Shared Iranian Asylum Seekers’ Immigration Files with Iran
description_short: A 2026 lawsuit alleges that U.S. officials shared Iranian asylum seekers’ confidential immigration files with Iran beginning in March 2025; DHS denies it.
description_medium: A July 2026 complaint by the Iranian American Legal Defense Fund alleges that the Trump administration adopted a policy in March 2025 to give Iran confidential immigration-file information about Iranian asylum seekers. The complaint says ICE and Iranian officials held monthly meetings to share records. CNN reported the suit and quoted a DHS spokesperson denying the allegation. These are allegations, not court findings; the complaint seeks declaratory and injunctive relief.
description_long: On July 7, 2026, the Iranian American Legal Defense Fund filed a complaint in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia through Public Citizen. The complaint alleges that the Trump administration adopted a policy in March 2025 to provide the Iranian government with confidential immigration-file information about Iranians seeking asylum in the United States. It says ICE and Iranian officials held monthly meetings to share records of people in ICE custody and that officials also sent or hand-delivered files. The complaint alleges that hundreds of Iranian detainees seeking asylum were affected and argues that disclosure could endanger applicants and relatives; those claims have not been adjudicated. CNN reported the complaint and quoted a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson saying the allegations that ICE shared asylum application records with Iran were false. The complaint asks the court for declaratory and injunctive relief, so no finding of unlawful sharing or resulting persecution is established here. The evidence is limited to Iranian asylum seekers and the Iranian government. The supplied date of March 1 is only a month-level anchor: the complaint says March 2025, not a specific day. The broader frozen claim about sharing detailed information with multiple foreign governments and documented targeting cases is not supported by these sources and is excluded.
date_precision: month; the complaint identifies March 2025 but not a day, and 2025-03-01 is an anchor only
